questions.stem: The TAP is the plane superficial to transversus abdominis, the ____ muscle of the anterolateral abdominal wall.
questions.answer: innermost

questions.stem: In the TAP plane, what do the intercostal, subcostal and L1 nerves form when they link up?
questions.answer: An upper and a lower TAP plexus

questions.stem: Which intercostal nerves does a subcostal TAP block cover?
Which nerves does a lateral TAP block cover?
Which spinal dermatome level does the umbilicus correspond to?
Which TAP block approach is needed to cover L1, which the lateral TAP block misses?
The quadratus lumborum (QL) lies ____ to psoas major, in the posterior abdominal wall.
questions.answer: dorsolateral

questions.stem: To which rib does the quadratus lumborum (QL) muscle attach?
Which lumbar transverse processes does the quadratus lumborum (QL) muscle attach to?
The thoracolumbar fascia (TLF) has anterior, middle and ____ layers, all continuous with the fused internal oblique/transversus aponeurosis.
questions.answer: posterior

questions.stem: Between which bony landmarks does the lateral raphe of the thoracolumbar fascia (TLF) run?
questions.answer: Iliac crest to 12th rib

questions.stem: Which three nerves cross the quadratus lumborum (QL) between the muscle and transversalis fascia?
questions.answer: Iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal and subcostal nerves

questions.stem: How many lumbar arteries on each side run behind psoas and QL, and end in the TAP?
On deep inspiration, the lower pole of the kidney can reach which lumbar level?
Which other block shares its indications with quadratus lumborum (QL) blocks?
For exploratory laparotomy with a midline incision, how should TAP blocks be placed?
TAP, TQL and QL1 blocks are which type of block, so they need large volumes?
What is the minimum local anaesthetic volume for each TAP block?
Some experts use what volume range of local anaesthetic for each TAP block?
What mainly determines systemic absorption of local anaesthetic after a TAP block?
Which needle is used for a single-shot TAP block?
What length of needle is used for a single-shot TAP block?
Which catheter gauge range is used for TAP block catheters?
Which needle is used to insert a TAP block catheter?
questions.answer: 10-cm Tuohy needle

questions.stem: What does a TAP block cover within the abdomen?
How long can a TAP block take to reach full sensory effect?
Which TAP block complication carries a risk of bowel or other visceral injury?
questions.answer: Intraperitoneal injection

questions.stem: Which probe is used for a lateral TAP block?
In a lateral TAP block, where and how is the probe placed?
questions.answer: Axial in the midaxillary line, between the costal margin and iliac crest

questions.stem: Which three abdominal wall muscles are identified on ultrasound for a lateral TAP block?
questions.answer: External oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis

questions.stem: Which plane is the target for a lateral TAP block?
options: Between internal oblique and transversus abdominis
Between external oblique and rectus sheath

questions.stem: In a lateral TAP block, where is the needle inserted?
The landmark lateral TAP technique enters through which anatomical triangle?
In the landmark lateral TAP technique, how is the needle oriented at the skin just above the iliac crest?
In the landmark lateral TAP technique, what does the first pop mark?
questions.answer: Passage through external oblique into the external/internal oblique plane

questions.stem: In the landmark lateral TAP technique, what does the second pop mark?
questions.answer: Passage through internal oblique fascia into the TAP

questions.stem: What volume of long-acting local anaesthetic is injected in the landmark lateral TAP technique?
In the landmark lateral TAP technique, in what aliquot size is the local anaesthetic injected after aspiration?
In what position is the patient for a subcostal TAP block?
In a subcostal TAP block, where should the probe lie?
questions.answer: Along the lower costal margin, as medial and cranial as possible

questions.stem: In a subcostal TAP block, which structures are seen on ultrasound from superficial to deep?
questions.answer: Rectus abdominis, posterior rectus sheath and transversus abdominis

questions.stem: What is the target plane of a subcostal TAP block?
options: Between rectus abdominis and its sheath
Between posterior rectus sheath and transversus abdominis

questions.stem: In a subcostal TAP block, where is the needle inserted and in which direction?
questions.answer: Above rectus near the midline, medial to lateral (or lateral to medial)

questions.stem: The oblique subcostal TAP block (OSTAP) is a variant of which block?
In an oblique subcostal TAP block (OSTAP), where does the needle start?
options: At the anterior superior iliac spine

questions.stem: Why is local anaesthetic injected in small increments during an OSTAP block?
questions.answer: To open the plane by hydrodissection

questions.stem: In an OSTAP block, when should the injection sequence be repeated?
questions.answer: Until the probe edge reaches the anterior iliac crest

questions.stem: How much local anaesthetic is used for hydrodissection medial to the semilunaris in OSTAP?
How much local anaesthetic remains for the internal oblique/transversus plane in OSTAP?
In OSTAP with a 10-cm needle, how often did the needle need withdrawing and reinserting?
For bilateral oblique subcostal TAP blocks, which local anaesthetic regimen was used?
The anterior TAP block is the same as which other block?
questions.answer: Ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric block

questions.stem: Which probe is used for a posterior TAP block?
In a posterior TAP block, where is the probe placed and how is it moved?
questions.answer: Axial in the midaxillary line, slid back to the most posterior limit of the internal oblique/transversus plane

questions.stem: In a posterior TAP block, where is the needle inserted and which way is it advanced?
questions.answer: At the midaxillary line, advanced backwards to the posterior end of the TAP

questions.stem: Which probe type and orientation are used to see the lateral wall muscles and QL in a QL block?
questions.answer: Low-frequency curved array, transverse

questions.stem: Which patient position is preferred for quadratus lumborum (QL) blocks?
Which quadratus lumborum block is the lateral, type 1 approach?
Which nerve branches does QL1 mainly block?
questions.answer: Lateral cutaneous branches of iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal and subcostal nerves

questions.stem: Which quadratus lumborum block is the posterior, type 2 approach?
In a posterior QL block, what should appear between latissimus dorsi and quadratus lumborum?
questions.answer: The LIFT

questions.stem: Which quadratus lumborum block is the anterior transmuscular (TQL) approach?
Which structure forms the stem of the shamrock sign in a transmuscular QL block?
Spread from a QL block to the thoracic paravertebral space aims to cover which levels?
Which nerve branches does the external oblique intercostal (EOI) block target?
options: Both anterior and lateral cutaneous branches

questions.stem: Which intercostal nerve levels does the external oblique intercostal (EOI) block target?
Where is the probe placed for an external oblique intercostal (EOI) block?
options: Over the 6th rib at the midclavicular line
Just medial to the anterior axillary line at the 6th rib
Over the iliac crest at the posterior axillary line
Below the umbilicus at the midline

questions.stem: What are the advantages of the external oblique intercostal (EOI) block?
questions.answer: Bony backstop, catheter possible, far from the surgical incision
